---
title: "Usage"
subtitle: "Workflow, options, margins after suest2, and the rules for weights, survey data, and MI"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

```stata
suest2 model1name model2name [, options]
```

*model#name* are stored estimates. Store each model with `estimates store`
before running `suest2`.

## The workflow

Fit each model, store it, combine, then do the post-estimation you want on
the combined system. For most applications, fit the models with `vce(robust)`
or `vce(cluster varname)`, so that the `suest2` standard errors match the
individual models' exactly.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear
drop if missing(union, wage, ttl_exp, collgrad, age, south)

quietly logit union c.age##i.collgrad i.south, vce(robust)
estimates store m1
quietly logit union c.age##i.collgrad i.south c.wage c.ttl_exp, vce(robust)
estimates store m2

suest2 m1 m2
<</dd_do>>
```

## What the combined results contain

The combined results are ordinary `e()` results: `e(b)` holds both models'
coefficients, one equation per model (named *model_depvar*, as in official
`suest`), and `e(V)` holds their joint covariance matrix including the
cross-model blocks. Any command that works on `e(b)` and `e(V)` works here.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
test [m1_union]1.collgrad = [m2_union]1.collgrad
nlcom ([m1_union]1.collgrad - [m2_union]1.collgrad) / [m1_union]1.collgrad
<</dd_do>>
```

`suest2` also stores what it did: `e(suest2_nmodels)`, the model names
`e(suest2_model#)`, each model's command `e(suest2_cmd#)`, and the route
flags `e(suest2_pweight)` and `e(suest2_svy)`; the full list is in the
[help file](help.html#stored).

## margins after suest2

A bare `margins` evaluates the default response for every constituent model.
To work with one model, name it in `predict()` with `model()`, together with
the prediction statistic:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
margins, dydx(age) predict(model(m1) pr)
margins, dydx(age) predict(model(m2) pr)
<</dd_do>>
```

`at()`, `over()`, `post`, and the other standard `margins` options work when
the constituent command supports the requested prediction, and inference uses
the complete joint covariance matrix. For multi-category models an outcome
is selected the same way, e.g. `predict(model(o1) pr outcome(3))`; for
multilevel models, `predict(model(me1) mu fixedonly)`.

Because the joint covariance is there, `margins, post` followed by `lincom`
or [`metest`](../metest/index.html) tests a marginal effect across the two
models -- which is what [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html) automates:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age
<</dd_do>>
```

## Options

| Option | Purpose |
|:--|:--|
| `cluster(varname)` | Cluster the joint covariance on *varname*. |
| `vce(robust)`, `robust` | Request the route's robust covariance. |
| `vce(cluster varname)` | Same as `cluster(varname)`. |
| `level(#)` | Confidence level; the default is 95. |
| `dir` | Pass through the official `suest` display option. |
| `eform(string)` | Exponentiated coefficients where applicable, with *string* as the column label, e.g. `eform("Odds ratio")`. The argument is required. |
| `minus(string)` | The official `suest` minus convention when supported; passed verbatim. |
| `regressml` | The official `suest` ML-regression convention when supported. |
| `svy` | Pass through the official `suest` survey option when supported. Does not replace fitting each survey model with the `svy:` prefix. |
| `nowarn` | Suppress the note printed when a model was not fit with `vce(robust)`. |

Specify only one of `cluster()`, `vce()`, and `robust`. Panel models cluster
at the panel identifier by default and multilevel models at the common
highest-level grouping variable; a larger cluster may be requested only when
the panels or groups are nested within it.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
suest2 m1 m2, eform("Odds ratio") nowarn
<</dd_do>>
```

## Weights, survey data, and multiple imputation

**Survey data.** For weighted analyses and complex samples, `svyset` the data
and fit each model with the `svy:` prefix, then pass the stored names to
`suest2` without a prefix. The design comes from `svyset`; do not specify
`cluster()`, `vce()`, or `robust` on `suest2`. All models must use the same
subpopulation specification, and replicate-weight VCEs are not supported.

**Pweights.** Pweighted systems support `regress`, `logit`/`logistic`,
`probit`, `poisson`, `nbreg`, `ologit`, `oprobit`, and `mlogit`, which may be
combined. The weights must agree on observations shared by the estimation
samples. Request system clustering with `cluster()` on `suest2`.

**Multiple imputation.** Fit and store each model with `mi estimate, post:`,
then pass the stored names to `suest2`. It re-estimates the constituents
jointly within each imputation and pools the system with Rubin's rules; the MI
data and all variables used must remain unchanged. Use `mimrgns` or
`mecompare` for post-estimation; ordinary `predict` and `margins` are not
available after MI pooling. The supported families are listed in the
[help file](help.html#weights).

## Supported estimators

The [help file](help.html#estimators) lists the supported families in full:
the ordinary single-level models (`regress` through `biprobit`, including
`gologit2`, `ivregress 2sls`, `fracreg`, `betareg`, `ivprobit`, and
`ivtobit`), the panel models (`xtreg`, `xtlogit`, `xtprobit`, `xtologit`,
`xtoprobit`, `xtmlogit`, `xtpoisson`, `xtnbreg`, `xtcloglog`, with the
estimators supported for each), and the multilevel models (`mixed`,
`melogit`, `meprobit`, `mecloglog`, `mepoisson`, `menbreg`, `meologit`,
`meoprobit`, `mestreg`, and `meglm` for the listed family-link pairs).

## Fixed effects and correlated random effects

Fixed-effects (`fe`) models have known problems for marginal effects,
especially with categorical outcomes. `xtreg, cre` is not supported, but the
identical correlated-random-effects (Mundlak) specification is: include each
time-varying predictor's panel mean alongside the predictor and fit with the
`re` estimator.

```stata
bysort id: egen mean_x = mean(x)
xtreg y x mean_x i.d, re
```

The coefficient on `x` is the within-person ("fixed effect") estimate and the
coefficient on `mean_x` the between-person estimate. The same recipe applies
to any supported panel or multilevel family.

## Housekeeping: suest2_cleanup

Each `suest2` run leaves private copies of its constituent estimates stored,
and Stata caps stored estimation sets at 300. In a long session,
`suest2_cleanup, force` reclaims them while preserving your own stored
estimates; `mecompare` does this automatically at the start of each run. See
[suest2_cleanup](help-suest2_cleanup.html).
